title: Vibhishana's Counsel to Ravana
text:
Ravana, the king of Lanka, had carried off Sita, the wife of Rama. Now Rama had found where she was held, and an army of monkeys and bears stood on the shore ready to cross to the island. Ravana called his council. His ministers and generals flattered him and boasted that they would destroy Rama easily.

Only his younger brother Vibhishana spoke against the mood of the room. He reminded Ravana of the bad omens in the city and of what Hanuman, a single messenger, had already done when he set Lanka on fire. Taking another man's wife was a wrong, he said, and the way to save the kingdom was to return Sita to Rama.

Ravana's son Indrajit mocked Vibhishana as a coward. Ravana himself grew furious. He accused his brother of envying him and of siding with the enemy, and said that if anyone else had spoken like that he would have killed him on the spot. Vibhishana rose, told Ravana he had spoken only for his good, and left Lanka with four companions. He crossed to Rama, who welcomed him.

In the war that followed, Ravana's sons and brothers fell one by one, and finally Ravana himself. Vibhishana was crowned king of Lanka.
lesson: The people who disagree with you in the meeting are often the ones looking out for you. If you punish honest counsel, you will soon hear only what you want to hear.
date: c. 5th century BC to 3rd century AD
